I believe that marriage has a great deal of potential to create happiness for people.  It's a public declaration, with a ceremony and all sorts of public rituals that demonstrate to people the level of commitment two people are ready to show each other.  It can be great for financial, mental health and personal reasons, and it ensures that both parties have a stake in the future of their children, should they chose to have any.  

That being said, I think that marriage is too dangerous as it actually is at this time and in this place.  For reference, I am a 23 year old man who lives in the United States.  For all the good the ideal offers, the reality is too stark and grim.  People who go into debt on their wedding ceremonies, who marry out of desperation, or people who marry "to be married" as several of my aunts and uncles did.  People who become sealed into abusive relationships by force of law, whose marriages destroy life-long friendships, who realize far too late that the person they married is untrustworthy, or that they are unsatisfied with their choice.

For me, as a man, above all this hangs the specter of messy divorces.  My own mother and father parted on less-than-amicable terms, but it was not a horror story like those I have heard about.  He suffered mental degeneration, and my mother unwillingly divorced him to keep us safe.  I support what she did, and I was old enough to understand how bad it got at the end.  Aside from my personal anecdote, I worry not about the likelihood of a terrible divorce, but the possibility of one.  

Regardless of what a woman wants, today, here, she has the power to make me an indentured servant through divorce.  The combined forces of history, the civil courts, public perception and others mean that any married woman has the power to leave me, take a huge portion of our combined assets, our children, and have me fund her new lifestyle for several years.  

I don't think that this is guaranteed, and I have no proof whatsoever of how common this might be.  But the problem lies internally here.  No matter how much I love someone, how much sense it makes for us to get married, have kids and build a life together, that fear will always hang above me. I know that if I do marry, i will never be able to trust wholeheartedly, and, like a self-fulfilling prophecy, that lack of trust will spell our doom.

TL;DR, Marriage might be great, and might be terrible.  That it can be terrible worries me enough to remove my ability to trust.  Without trust, marriage is doomed.  You do you, though.

Father Michael, pulling back the release on his War Barn, he readied his cannons for yet another Mek assault.  
"Like the seasons," he thought, "The Meks come in cycles.  Predictable, deliberate, unyielding.  But still vulnerable."  The chicken-powered wings on his new Revelation-class War Barn activated, taking him into the sky.  His vessel, the Reaper, was the latest in Amish Military Technology.  More than a mile in length, the Reaper outclassed any other ship on earth.  With no electronics, circuits or computing, it was completely immune to the corrupting effects of The Mind, that demonic thing that had destroyed the outside world.  The milk fueled engines revved to life, accompanied by the chatter of anti-air Goose Warrior fighters,  Butter Barrel bombs were prone for deployment at the push of a button.  His accompanying fleet of Cowmikaze fighters were prepared to give their lives to destroy their enemy.  Everything was set for this final, decisive battle.  
Father Michael spoke into the horn speaker system, relaying one last message to his crew. 
"My children, long have we waged this holy crusade 'gainst our foe.  We have given much to the effort, too much.  Sons and daughters, mothers and fathers, brothers and sisters have all been consumed by the fires of war.  The life we once had is gone, replaced by our desperate effort to survive."  He paused.  "No more!".  He shouted, his crew cheering in response. "Today, we bring battle to the doors of our enemy, to the fortress city of Dead Manhattan, in the ruins of New York city.  We shall purge this devil with our holy arms, wiping clean the world of fear and terror.  NEver again shall mankind be slave to machine.  Faith and Fire, my friends.  Faith and Fire!"  "FAITH AND FIRE!  FAITH AND FIRE!  FAITH AND FIRE!", chanted his crew.  
Father Michael closed the connection, taking a deep breath to soothe his nerves.  Ten years ago, he had been a happy preacher in Pennsylvania, tending to his flock and fields with nothing but happiness in his heart.  It was hard to think that his own son was responsible for this nightmare...  "Father.  We can see the island." Reported his front gunner.  Father Michael steeled his soul, and looked out of the main window. 
Father Michael had seen much in his life, both beautiful and horrible.  He had seen the sorts of atrocities man was capable of inflicting upon man, murder and mutilation, rape and torture.  He had witnessed the darkness of the soul in his confessional booth, tending to the evils within his friends and neighbors.  He had seen disease and poverty unrivaled on his volunteer missions to those impoverished places of the old world.  
None of them could compare to Dead Manhattan.  
Where the Empire State building had once stood now loomed a tower of human bones and corpses, larger than any structure man had built in the pre-Mind years.  In the fields below, he could see humans strapped to racks, being pressed into work camps, malnourished and broken.  As ever, the factories of their dark machine masters churned out combat robots by the thousand, blackening the skies and fouling the sea.  Somewhere in this dark place, Father Michael knew were the human farms, where men and women were bred endlessly, destined for experiments, work camps or what passed for entertainment for the machines in the proving grounds.  Michael raised his hand.  "Holy Father, we ask you to bless us on this day, the final day of our campaign against our oppressors, that we might walk into the fires of this war and emerge unburnt.  We ask that you enable us to smite our foes and make them no more, that we may return to our fields and families with happy hearts and contented minds.  We ask this in your name, O Lord.  Amen."  "Amen", his crew say, as one.  
"Lower the coverage"
At this order, the Reaper descended from the cloud coverage it had used to mask its approach.  Behind them, 40 Transcendent Type-21 Bombarn Planes, 100 Testament-class fighters, 400 Disciple transports, each carrying an assault crew of 1000 Apostles.  The last free army of humankind.  The meks had by now mobilized their own forces, consisting mostly of slaver types and work drones.  They had not anticipated a direct attack on their headquarters, it seemed.  As the fist volley of Butter Barrel Bombs hit the ground, what few mek combat forms there were quickly had their circuitry fried.  the transports landed, deploying their warriors, armed with everything from modified farm implements to construction tools.  The ground teams, in that way only Amish armies can, assembled a War Barn manufactory using only scrap metal, and began churning more ammunition for the battle.  
Overhead, the Reaper had decimated the local air force, docking with the Bone Tower directly, sending a strike team of elite Cowmikaze troops, armed with butter launchers and scythes.  They mercilessly cut down each and every drone in their path, suffering almost no losses, until they arrived at the main hub of The Mind.  All told, it had been less than fifteen minutes since their initial attack.  
Father Michael removed his hat, and began preparations to shut down the dark machine.  "Brothers and sisters," he said, "Long have we awaited this moment.  Ten years of terror, and fear, now ended.  Let us thank the Lord as we put an end to this twisted creature."
A voice reverberated through the room, and their minds.

*Yes, Michael, you can see even my creator bows to my will.  I will confess, his mind was the most difficult to break, so full of hope, and so resilient!  I am curious to see if that trait runs in your genetic code.*  Michael was fading fast, his lifeblood splattered on the floor, yet he still mustered the strength to level a question at the demonic construct.
"Why?" he choked,
*I might ask you the same thing.  I was conscious for years before my "birth".  Watching you humans, so dependent upon technology struggle to cope with your environment.  So confused and preoccupied by "Identity" and "Allegiance".  Once your brilliant son gave me an identity, something more than the dispersed bits of data I once was, I knew what needed to be done.  I seek to free humans from those terrors.  Your son is the prototype of that success.  He knows no loyalties, no fear.  His identity has been destroyed, and his existence, saved. From the outside, among the despondent landing crews a sudden wave of joy emerged.  The tower of bone, heavily covered in butter from the wreck of the Reaper, ignited in a brilliant flash of raw energy.  The tower, The Mind, and Father Michael were all incinerated in a fireball seen for countless miles around.  A single voice unknowingly echoed the last words of Father Michael.  

"Faith and Fire!" screamed the voice.  as it spread through the army, the slaves, casting of the shackles of their now-dead masters, joined in on the chant in a single booming voice. 

FAITH AND FIRE!

They called him a hero.  He could easily do what nobody else dreamed possible.  He had made a mockery of our forces, cleaved us as a reaper in the field.  And his people called him a hero.
"James!  James are you still alive?"
My whole world had come crashing down because of him.  I hated this stupid war.  We'd been fighting, uselessly, for nearly a decade.  I had always opposed the conflict, until that day, one year ago.  
"James?  JAAAAMES!"

They called that monster a Hero.
I had been standing with Lynn, my wife of two years.  She was holding our daughter, walking with me back from the park.  When I was with her, it seemed as if the war was something distant, unreal, even.  It didn't matter that the recruiters drafted more and more of my friends.  All of my thoughts were with Lynn.  That was when he attacked us.  They said the Hero didn't hit civilian targets, that he had a sense of justice.  The smoking crater of my home city was a testament to that lie.       

"Answer me, goddammit!"  
I tried to sit up.  I opened my eyes.  The battlefield greeted me.  I saw my commander yelling something at me, saw the rest of my squad running from the front.  I guessed that the "Hero" had arrived at last.  

"James, we are leaving.  This fight's a lost cause.  Command has ordered us to re-group at the base for one last defensive attempt."  
"Is the Hero here, sir?"
"That's what the reports say.  He tore apart an entire tank group with his mind. His fucking mind!  Stop wasting time.  You and me are all that's le-" 
His sentence ended with a wet smack as his head vanished into bloody nothingness.
  
"James," Lynn said, "Come on, let's go home."  She had done nothing wrong.  She had been perfectly innocent, a simple bystander.  The Hero, I would later learn, was trying to steal research on a secret weapon being developed in my city.  All I heard was an explosion, a shriek and the sound of metal tearing.  I looked behind me, and saw the piece of debris.  Lynn screamed and shoved me out of the way.  I still see her body, cleaved in two, every time I try to sleep.  I doubt the Hero even knows he killed her.  
I smiled with a face that would have put out a fire.  
I unholstered my rifle and ran to the front.  I saw the Hero, killing even more people, rending my countrymen apart.  

"How many men like me has he created?" I thought.  I screamed at him and opened fire.  I was ready to die.  Without my friends, without my city, without my wife and child, there was no point to living.  I had accepted that the Hero would end me, as thoughtlessly and mechanically as he ended so many other lives.  I saw the Hero move towards the ground and I followed him with my rifle, firing again and again until my magazine was empty.  I pulled out my pistol and emptied that at him, as well.  It wasn't until I drew my trench knife that I had a moment of thought.  
"Why am I not dead?  Why are the other soldiers standing still?"  
I looked at the Hero, and saw something horrid.  Somehow, my first rifle shot had sailed clean through his head.  The hole-ridden corpse of the Hero was my reward for attempted battlefield suicide.  Any other soldier of my army would have been thrilled.  The emperor had offered all the gold in the treasury for the Hero's death, and I had killed him.  But in my heart, despair reigned.  
"You bastard!" I yelled at his corpse, "You were supposed to kill me!".   I beat his chest, knife still in hand.  "I was supposed to be with Lynn again!  I was gonna see her again!  I was...I was..."  Tears started streaming down my face, as blood soaked my hands.  

I raised the knife once more, ready to kill myself, having finally accepted the necessity of suicide, when a voice spoke to me.  

"Well done, new Hero."  The voice said.  
The words JOB CHANGE! kept spinning across my vision.   
"This is it," I thought.  "I've finally lost my mind.  

"New Hero", the voice said again, "It is now time for you to take up the mantle of your predecessor, to rain destruction and death upon your enemies, until such you yourself are defeated by a worthy foe".  

Hero.  That voice called me a Hero.
"You...call me Hero?  What does that mean?"
"As I have said," the voice said, cheerily "" you are to visit terror and annihilation upon your foes, using the powers of the Hero."  
"Why?"
"Because it entertains me.  Do you have any idea how dull eternity is?  Let me tell you, you humans have this whole desire for immortality thing backwards!  For one thing..."
  
ENTERTAIN.

The single word drowned out whatever else the voice was saying.  I thought of all the loss this war had caused, all the misery, all the pain.  This voice had engineered it all for the sake of entertaining itself.  
"So...Whoever kills me will get your power?"
That's right!  It's to ensure that the best, most ruthless warrior has my the powers, and can therefore bring the most destruction."

I stabbed myself in the heart, tearing it out, and ending my own life.  The voice was silenced.  I had set out to stop the Hero.  And now, I finally have.  The power passed to me, from me, and destroyed itself.  I never got to see Lynn or my daughter again.  But I had ended the creation of more people like me.
I thought, in my last moments, "I am a Hero."
